displayPattern: Dishwasher display shows 5C (also shown as SC, 5E or SE on some models)
meaning: Drain error: the dishwasher can't drain.
causes: Blocked sink drain or garbage disposal
Drain hose pinched, kinked, or missing an air gap or high loop
Dirty or incorrectly reassembled drain and filter area
diySteps: Check the sink drain and garbage disposal: if you use a disposal, make sure it is clear of food waste; if the dishwasher drains directly, look down the drain for a visible blockage; if the dishwasher or disposal was recently installed, make sure the disposal cap has been removed

Check the drain hose: right after installation, the most common cause is the dishwasher sitting on its own drain hose and pinching it shut. Also check the hose has an air gap or a "high loop" (part of the hose above its sink connection), and is not kinked or bent
Run water in the connected sink for about 30 seconds; if the sink does not drain, the problem is in the home's plumbing, so call a plumber
Clean the drain and filter area (removable parts are covered in your user manual) and reassemble it correctly, taking care with sharp debris
Make sure your drain line is not frozen; if it might be, let the area warm up (Samsung notes frozen lines are not covered under warranty service)
safetyNote: Switch the dishwasher off at its breaker before you reach into the base or remove a filter or cover, and let the tub and water cool after a cycle. Watch for sharp debris. Pump, heater, valve and control-board repairs belong to a qualified appliance technician.
proAdvice: If the dishwasher still won't drain after these checks, Samsung says to request service through its Support Center.
sourceTitle: Samsung dishwasher is displaying an error code (Samsung Support)
